issues.description: Pixel byte-size inconsistency: the problem statement states pixels are effectively 32-bit (rounded from 24-bit) and main/position calculation in the solution uses 4 bytes per pixel (offset y*1920*4 + x*4), but the implemented set_pixel in the solution computes x*3 (uses 3 bytes per pixel). This mismatch will cause incorrect address calculation when writing the pixel (writes at wrong offsets) and will confuse students about whether pixels are 3 or 4 bytes wide.
issues.suggested_fix: Make pixel byte-size consistent across artifacts. Since the problem statement and main position calculation use 32-bit (4 bytes) per pixel, change the set_pixel implementation to compute offsets using 4 bytes/pixel. For example, replace the x*3 multiplication with x*4 (use mov edx, 4; mul edx or shl eax, 2) and ensure the comment reflects 32-bit pixel depth. Ensure the final address calculation adds display_start to (y*1920*4 + x*4) and then writes ecx to that address. This keeps set_pixel consistent with the position calculation in main and the problem description.
